excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content:
There is an issue related to the data section in EOF. See "Account for constructor arguments during on-chain contract creation" in https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/eof1-checklist.

The thing is that data is used to pass arguments to contract constructors. Traditionally, the ABI-encoded values are appended to the initcode. In the EOF the data size is in the EOF header and it must match the exact number of bytes.
1. This means all tx tools must be aware of that and not only append the constructor arguments but also patch the EOF header with the correct data size. This issue we were aware of but considered "acceptable".
2. Today we realized the same situation is also for using `CREATE` instruction, i.e. when a contract creates a new contract. The EOF contract must also patch the EOF container with initcode for `CREATE` with the correct data size. This is not horrible but also not trivial considering EVM works with `uint256` and EOF keeps sizes as `uint16`.
3. It's getting even worse with `CREATE2` for which users may want to predict the address before creating an account. And the address depends on the hash of the EOF initcode. <@427011130318389248> says it may be impossible to keep this use-case working in general case.

One solution we considered some time ago was to just allow any bytes after the code, without specifying the size. Definitely not very elegant but makes all the use-cases above work and EOF-agnostic.

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content:
1. You have some kind of meta-param "total container size" living outside. You have to take the value from somewhere. E.g. memory buffer size, file size, database field size, etc.
2. With the current EOF format you can stream EOFs just by concatenating them. After, you need at least tar-like encoding.
